questions.q: Write the central form of the equation of a circle with centre at (-3, 4) and radius 5 units.
questions.a: (x + 3)² + (y - 4)² = 25. A wrong answer like (x - 3)² + (y + 4)² = 25 reveals the student is not careful with signs: the central form is (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r², so if h = -3, then x - (-3) = x + 3. This is the most frequent sign error at this level.

questions.q: The equation x² + y² - 6x + 8y - 11 = 0 represents a circle. Find its centre and radius. Explain why the centre is NOT (3, -4).
questions.a: Centre = (3, -4), radius = 6. The general form is x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 with centre (-g, -f). Here 2g = -6 ⇒ g = -3, so -g = 3; 2f = 8 ⇒ f = 4, so -f = -4. A student who says centre is (-3, 4) has confused g with -g — they read the coefficient of x as g instead of 2g, or forgot the minus sign in the centre formula.

questions.q: Find the equation of the circle having the line segment joining A(1, 2) and B(5, 6) as a diameter.
questions.a: Using diameter form: (x - 1)(x - 5) + (y - 2)(y - 6) = 0 ⇒ x² + y² - 6x - 8y + 17 = 0. A wrong answer like (x - 3)² + (y - 4)² = 8 (using midpoint as centre and half the distance as radius) is mathematically correct but misses the point: the diameter form is faster and directly uses the given endpoints without computing midpoint and distance. If a student cannot write the diameter form, they have not internalized the angle-in-semicircle property.

questions.q: Determine whether the equation 2x² + 2y² - 8x + 12y + 26 = 0 represents a real circle, a point circle, or no real locus. Justify your answer.
questions.a: Divide by 2: x² + y² - 4x + 6y + 13 = 0. Here g = -2, f = 3, c = 13. g² + f² - c = 4 + 9 - 13 = 0. Since g² + f² - c = 0, it represents a point circle (a single point at (2, -3)). A student who says "no real circle" or "radius = 0 so not a circle" misunderstands: a point circle IS a valid degenerate circle (radius zero). The condition g² + f² - c > 0 is for a real circle with positive radius; = 0 gives a point circle; < 0 gives no real locus.

questions.q: A student claims: "The equation x² + y² + 4x - 6y + 20 = 0 represents a circle with centre (-2, 3) and radius √20." Evaluate this claim and correct any errors.
questions.a: The claim is false. Centre is correctly (-2, 3) because g = 2 ⇒ -g = -2, f = -3 ⇒ -f = 3. But radius² = g² + f² - c = 4 + 9 - 20 = -7 < 0. Since radius² is negative, there is NO real circle — the equation has no real locus. The student incorrectly used c = 20 as radius² instead of computing g² + f² - c. This reveals confusion between the constant term c and the radius formula.

questions.q: Create a real-world problem (with Indian context) that requires finding the equation of a circle in general form, where the given data is the centre and a point on the circumference. Provide the full solution.
questions.a:
Example: A circular jogging track in a Delhi park has its centre at the flagpole located at (2, -3). A water fountain on the track is at (5, 1). Find the equation of the track in general form.
Solution: Centre (2, -3), point (5, 1) ⇒ radius² = (5-2)² + (1+3)² = 9 + 16 = 25.
Central form: (x - 2)² + (y + 3)² = 25 ⇒ x² + y² - 4x + 6y - 12 = 0.
A poor answer would give only the central form or compute radius incorrectly. The key is converting to general form (x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0) as asked, and verifying g² + f² - c = 4 + 9 + 12 = 25 > 0.
